inclusion.title: Inclusion
inclusion.body: We believe the handball court is a place for everyone. By intentionally bringing together youth from diverse socioeconomic, cultural, and geographic backgrounds, we use sport to break down societal barriers. Our program guarantees a safe, welcoming, and respectful space where every young person feels valued and accepted.

youthLeadership.title: Youth leadership
youthLeadership.body: We are committed to shaping the leaders of tomorrow, on and off the court. Through targeted workshops, peer mentorship, and team activities, we equip young people with essential communication and decision-making skills, and encourage them to take initiative and become proactive role models in their communities.

empowerment.title: Empowerment
empowerment.body: Our program goes beyond the mechanics of handball; it is a catalyst for personal growth. By providing quality resources, dedicated coaching, and a platform for their voices to be heard, we give youth the confidence to realize their potential, set ambitious goals, and take control of their own futures.

resilience.title: Resilience
resilience.body: Sport is one of the greatest teachers of how to handle both victory and defeat. Through the physical and mental demands of training and tournaments, our youth learn to overcome adversity and bounce back from setbacks — strength that carries directly into their daily lives.

hero.intro: Play4Ward is a youth handball initiative that uses sport as a tool for personal development, confidence, and teamwork in a safe and inclusive setting.

story.title: Why we exist
story.body1: Play4Ward was founded by Rony Francillon and Vasty Jean François, who grew up playing handball in Haiti. In high school there was no sports field in their community and no money for shoes or gear. Their mother was already stretching to pay for a good education, so the Saturday sports academies many of their classmates attended stayed out of reach. They played anyway — goals made from backpacks, and a football standing in for a handball because their coach only had a few.
story.body2: Handball was barely known at their school, so it was never given much importance. Those conversations were frustrating, but out on the playing field that same group of friends found real community and belonging. That contrast is why Play4Ward exists. Young people in Jacmel who want to play still have little access to coached sport, proper equipment, or the leadership opportunities a team brings — so we are building the space we didn't have, and building it so everyone gets to take part, whatever their background.
story.photo: A Play4Ward training session in Jacmel

mv.mission: Our goal is to provide young people with a safe and inclusive space where handball serves as a tool to build confidence, teamwork, and essential life skills.
mv.vision: Our vision is to be the national home of youth handball in Haiti, where sport builds character, community, and champions.

items.title: Social inclusion
items.body: Our program creates a safe and respectful space where marginalized and underrepresented youth can connect, grow, and thrive alongside their peers — regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, religion, or socioeconomic background.

items.title: Positive youth development
items.body: We use sport to create structured, supportive environments where young people build confidence, discipline, teamwork, and a sense of belonging. Through consistent engagement and mentorship, we help guide youth toward healthy choices.

items.title: Civic engagement
items.body: We empower young people to form their own opinions, express themselves confidently, and make informed decisions — recognizing their role as active citizens who can contribute positively to their community and country.

why.title: A fast, team-based, accessible sport
why.intro: Many visitors, especially international ones, don't know handball well. Here's why we chose it:
points: Fast and accessible, with little equipment.
Suitable for girls and boys alike.
Great for building coordination, communication, and resilience.
Still underdeveloped in Haiti compared with other sports.
why.federation: Haiti has an officially recognized national handball federation and has been an International Handball Federation member since 2004 — placing Play4Ward within a legitimate national sporting ecosystem.

center.title: Handball Training Center
body: Our training sessions put a strong emphasis on collaboration, teamwork, and the ability to work harmoniously with people regardless of their cultural, economic, or social background. Because we believe in social inclusion through sport, these sessions are designed as safe, structured, and respectful spaces where marginalized and underrepresented youth can grow and thrive alongside their peers.

Young people play handball with high-quality gear in an adapted environment, and our coaching staff works to ensure every athlete has access to well-equipped facilities to safely explore their talents and build discipline. Ultimately these practices are not only about athletic excellence — they are a vehicle for self-confidence, a sense of belonging, and essential life skills.
center.who: Young people ages 13–18 interested in developing their handball and leadership skills.
expect: Teamwork and a willingness to grow
center.photo: Young athletes training at the Play4Ward centre

leadership.title: Growing beyond the court
leadership.intro: Beyond the court, our leadership, well-being, and personal development workshops create an inspiring and educational space.
body: These sessions let young people interact directly with players from the Haitian national selection and other inspiring community figures, connecting with mentors through storytelling. By sharing their own stories and listening to others, our youth align their visions and goals in a supportive setting.

That fosters a real sense of community and helps them see what they can accomplish together. Through consistent engagement and mentorship, we aim to forge character, break down social barriers, and guide young people toward healthy choices and positive personal growth.

outreach.title: Bringing handball to where young people live

tournaments.title: Play, represent, celebrate
tournaments.intro: We organize and take part in local and regional tournaments so young people can test their skills and teamwork.
body: They experience the thrill of the game both in their own neighbourhoods and in entirely new environments. These events go well beyond standard competition: they are a platform for our players to meet, compete, and share meaningful experiences with youth from different economic and social backgrounds.

By bridging those divides we champion social inclusion and respect for all, regardless of gender, religion, or socioeconomic status. Tournaments reinforce our vision of sport as a tool to build stronger communities, forge lasting friendships, and shape the champions of tomorrow — on and off the court.

sdg.intro: Play4Ward contributes to three of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. These are the goals our programming is built around.

items.title: Good health & well-being
items.body: Through regular handball practices and personal development workshops, we promote healthy lifestyles for our youth. By keeping young people physically active and mentally supported in a safe environment, we foster both physical fitness and emotional resilience, guiding them toward healthy choices.

items.title: Gender equality
items.body: We are committed to empowering girls and young women by ensuring equal access to our training sessions, mentorship programs, and leadership workshops. By promoting female participation in handball and breaking down gender stereotypes in sport, we create an environment where everyone has the opportunity to lead and succeed.

items.title: Reduced inequalities
items.body: By providing quality gear, coaching, and facilities to marginalized and underrepresented youth, we level the playing field. Our program deliberately brings together young people from diverse socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds — in practice and in tournaments — fostering mutual respect and breaking down societal barriers.
